logic_JU_2021.text: 24. "Brazil is the most popular country in football sport. Therefore, everyone in Brazil is a popular footballer." This argument commits fallacy of: (2021)
logic_JU_2021.explanation: The fallacy of division occurs when an argument illicitly concludes that an attribute of a whole (Brazil as a nation being renowned for football) must necessarily be true of its individual parts (every individual Brazilian).

logic_JU_2021.subject: Logic
logic_JU_2021.text: 25. "Is evil an inherent quality of the world? How could it be? What a wretched place this earth would be if it were." This is a good example for: (2021)
logic_JU_2021.explanation: Wishful thinking occurs when a person accepts or rejects a claim based on whether they want it to be true or false, rather than on evidence. Rejecting the notion of inherent evil simply because it would make the world a "wretched place" completely relies on emotional desire over factual assessment.

logic_JU_2021.subject: Logic
logic_JU_2021.text: 26. Which one of the following is Correct about fallacious passages? (2021)

options.text: A. Necessarily, they are inferential passage.
B. Necessarily, they are either bad inductive or deductive arguments.
C. Are constituted by statements with 'false' truth values.

logic_JU_2021.explanation: A fallacy is universally defined as a defect in an argument. Because an argument is an inferential passage (Option A) and a fallacious argument is mathematically a bad inductive or deductive argument (Option B), both statements accurately reflect formal definitions. However, fallacies can easily utilize premises with 'true' truth values (eliminating Option C), making 'All of the above' incorrect.

logic_JU_2021.subject: Logic
logic_JU_2021.text: 27. Against a person fallacy is committed when someone try to defeat other's claim by: (2021)

options.text: A. Coming up with a better counter claim.
B. Attacking the arguer's personality through which he can easily defeat his views.
C. Distorting the view of someone to make it susceptible for attack.
D. Applying a general rule to a specific case it was not intended to cover.

logic_JU_2021.explanation: The fallacy against the person (argumentum ad hominem) operates by directing an attack against the character, personality, or circumstances of the opponent rather than engaging with the logical content of their argument.

logic_JU_2021.subject: Logic
logic_JU_2021.text: 28. Which one is correct regarding fallacies of Weak Induction? (2021)

options.text: A. Committed when the premises are logically irrelevant to the conclusion.
B. Committed when the premises are sufficient to prove the conclusion.
C. Exclusively committed by Inductive arguments.
D. Committed when statements in the argumentation are misplaced.

logic_JU_2021.explanation: Fallacies of weak induction arise when the premises provide at least some shred of relevant evidence, but the connection between the premises and the conclusion is not strong enough to support the conclusion. Standard logic classifications explicitly categorize these as inductive fallacies because they mimic inductive probability but fail to meet the required strength.

logic_JU_2021.subject: Logic
logic_JU_2021.text: 29. Which one is incorrect? (2021)

options.text: A. Appeal to pity takes place when an arguer tries to get people to accept a conclusion by making them feel sorry for someone.
B. In the appeal to ignorance, the arguer basically says, "Look, there's no conclusive evidence on the issue at hand. So, you should accept my conclusion on this issue."
C. In Strawman, the premises of an argument do support a particular conclusion but not the conclusion that the arguer actually draws.
D. Equivocation is sliding between two or more different meanings of a single word or phrase that is important to the argument.

logic_JU_2021.explanation: Option C actually describes the 'missing the point' (ignoratio elenchi) fallacy, not the straw man fallacy. The straw man fallacy involves distorting or exaggerating an opponent's argument, defeating the distorted version, and then concluding that the original argument was defeated. Therefore, C is the incorrect statement.

logic_JU_2021.subject: Logic
logic_JU_2021.text: 30. You should believe in God's existence. Unless, you will be destined to suffer eternally at hell. (2021)
logic_JU_2021.explanation: This argument relies on the threat of severe harm (eternal suffering) rather than logical evidence to compel agreement. When a threat implicitly replaces a premise, it commits the fallacy of appeal to force.

logic_JU_2021.subject: Logic
logic_JU_2021.text: 31. Bill Gates gives millions of dollars to charitable causes every year. It must be the case that all wealthy people give huge amounts of money to charity every year ________ (2021)
logic_JU_2021.explanation: Drawing a universal conclusion about an entire group ('all wealthy people') based on an isolated, atypical, or very small sample (only Bill Gates) is the textbook definition of the hasty generalization fallacy.

logic_JU_2021.subject: Logic
logic_JU_2021.text: 32. Probably no life exists on Venus. Teams of scientists have conducted exhaustive studies of the planet's surface and atmosphere, and no living organisms have been found ________ (2021)
logic_JU_2021.explanation: While normally arguing from a lack of evidence commits the appeal to ignorance, an exception is made when qualified researchers conduct exhaustive, specialized searches and fail to find evidence. In this context, the absence of evidence becomes legitimate evidence of absence, making it a cogent inductive argument.

logic_JU_2021.subject: Logic
logic_JU_2021.text: 33. People who lack humility have no sense of beauty, because everyone who has a sense of beauty also has humility ________ (2021)
logic_JU_2021.explanation: The premise 'everyone who has a sense of beauty also has humility' is logically equivalent via contraposition to the conclusion 'People who lack humility have no sense of beauty.' Asserting a conclusion that merely restates the premise in different words commits the fallacy of begging the question (petitio principii).

logic_JU_2021.subject: Logic
logic_JU_2021.text: 34. A teacher is a human being. Thus, a good teacher is a good human being. (2021)
logic_JU_2021.explanation: The argument conflates two distinct meanings of the word 'good'. A 'good teacher' implies professional competence or pedagogical skill, whereas a 'good human being' refers to moral virtue. Shifting definitions midway through the argument constitutes equivocation.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 1. All invalid arguments commit formal fallacy.
logic_JU_1.explanation: Invalidity means that the conclusion does not follow necessarily from the premises, but the error may be formal or informal. A formal fallacy concerns the logical structure of an argument, whereas an informal fallacy results from problems such as relevance, ambiguity, or inadequate evidence.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 2. Some fallacious passages are inferential.
logic_JU_1.explanation: A fallacious passage can be inferential because it attempts to support a conclusion from premises while containing a defect in reasoning. The presence of an attempted inference distinguishes such a passage from a mere collection of unrelated statements.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 3. Fallacious arguments contain one or more factual errors in their form.
logic_JU_1.explanation: A fallacy is an error in reasoning, not necessarily an error in factual content. An argument can contain true statements and still be fallacious if its reasoning does not properly support the conclusion.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 4. Fallacious reasoning have a necessary deceiving characters.
logic_JU_1.explanation: In the terminology used for this course, fallacious reasoning has a deceptive character because it can make weak reasoning appear acceptable or persuasive. The deception does not require deliberate dishonesty by the person presenting the argument.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 5. Critical thinking helps us to investigate data, belief or facts accurately and partially.
logic_JU_1.explanation: Critical thinking requires accurate and impartial investigation of data, beliefs, and facts. A partial or biased investigation can distort the evaluation of evidence and therefore does not represent the proper aim of critical thinking.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 6. Which one of the following is ODD about critical thinking?

options.text: A. The intellect is equally important like the body in the due process of critical thinking
B. Being intelligent is sufficient by itself to be critical thinker
C. It is acquired by nature

logic_JU_1.explanation: The intended answer is A because critical thinking is principally an intellectual activity involving reasoning, analysis, evaluation, and reflection rather than an equal process involving the body. Intelligence alone is not sufficient for critical thinking, and critical-thinking ability involves developed habits and dispositions.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 7. Robert Ennis defined critical thinking as:

options.text: A. A journey to arrive at the most useful destinations while evaluating claims for scientific truth.
B. A reasonable and reflective thinking focusing on deciding what to believe or do.
C. An attitude of being disposed to consider in a thoughtful way.

logic_JU_1.explanation: Robert Ennis characterizes critical thinking as reasonable and reflective thinking focused on deciding what to believe or do. The definition emphasizes rational evaluation and reflection in reaching beliefs or decisions.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 8. Which one of the following statements is Correct?

options.text: A. Man is by nature rational being; thus, he/she is a critical thinker.
B. Critical thinking is to think by disregarding a society’s norm, value, law and tradition.
C. Critical thinking is less helpful to be successful in academic arena.
D. It is unsound to assume that everyone can be equally be a critical thinker.

logic_JU_1.explanation: Being naturally rational does not automatically make a person a critical thinker, and critical thinking does not require rejecting social norms, values, laws, or traditions. Critical thinking is useful in academic work, while people can differ in their development of critical-thinking skills and dispositions.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 9. One of the following is not among the characteristics of a critical thinker.
logic_JU_1.explanation: Gut feeling is an intuitive reaction rather than a defining characteristic of critical thinking. Critical thinkers are characterized by dispositions such as inquisitiveness and a willingness to examine evidence and alternatives carefully.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 10. Which one is ODD about fallacious passages?

options.text: A. The statements that constitute fallacious passages have “False” truth value, necessarily.
B. All bad arguments are fallacious, necessarily.
C. No other than inductive and deductive arguments can commit fallacy of any form.
D. Some cogent arguments commit fallacy.

logic_JU_1.explanation: The intended answer is C because fallacies are analyzed as defects in reasoning within arguments, while the other statements describe claims treated as incorrect within the course framework. In particular, fallaciousness does not require every statement in an argument to be false, and a cogent argument cannot simultaneously be fallacious in the relevant sense.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text:
11. “If you want to be a part of this team, I suggest that you put in some effort and start contributing more.”
This passage commits fallacy of:
logic_JU_1.explanation: The statement conditions continued membership in the team on complying with the demand to contribute more, implying an undesirable consequence for noncompliance. This makes the argument an appeal to force rather than an attack on a person, an appeal to popularity, or an appeal to pity.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 12. A fallacy based on the idea that if many people agree on the same point, it must be true is:
logic_JU_1.explanation: The bandwagon fallacy treats widespread acceptance as evidence that a claim is true. The number of people who believe a proposition does not by itself establish the truth of that proposition.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 13. “If my brother likes to eat a lot of pizza and French fries, and he is healthy, I can say that pizza and French fries are healthy and don't really make a person fat.” Fallacy of this passage is:
logic_JU_1.explanation: The conclusion generalizes from the experience of one person to pizza and French fries in general. A single healthy individual is insufficient evidence for a broad claim about the effects of these foods, which makes the reasoning a hasty generalization.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 14. A fallacy that creates the illusion; inadequate premises provide support for a conclusion is:
logic_JU_1.explanation: Suppressed evidence occurs when relevant evidence is omitted, making the stated premises appear to provide stronger support for the conclusion than they actually do. The omitted information may materially weaken the argument or support a different conclusion.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 15. Identify the habitual use of immature defense mechanisms when our worldviews are challenged:
logic_JU_1.explanation: Absolutism involves treating one's own beliefs as fixed and unquestionable, making it difficult to reconsider them when challenged. Egocentrism centers on one's own perspective, ethnocentrism centers on one's culture, and conformism centers on agreement with a group.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 16. “All living beings come from other living beings. Therefore, the first forms of life must have come from a living being. That living being is God.” The logical fault of this argumentation is:
logic_JU_1.explanation: The argument shifts the application of the concept of living beings when moving from the general claim about existing life to the supposed first form of life. This change in meaning creates an equivocation rather than establishing the conclusion from the stated premise.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text:
17. Which types of fallacy commit in the following dialogue?
Dawit: I always wondered, why doesn’t God just destroy Satan? He destroyed every living being on the earth (besides those on the ark) for much less of a crime.
Tomas: Jesus loves you!
logic_JU_1.explanation: The intended classification is strawman because Tomas replaces the issue raised by Dawit with a simplified response that does not address the actual reasoning challenge. The response therefore fails to engage with the position being questioned and substitutes a different issue.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 18. The best way to deal with group centered thinking is:

options.text: A. Being reluctant to accept the views of others
B. Disregarding societal values and authorities at all
C. Develop habits of independent thinking
D. Accepting the views of one’s preferred group
E. C and D are answers

logic_JU_1.explanation: Independent thinking helps a person evaluate claims using evidence and reasoning rather than simply accepting the position of a preferred group. Independent thinking does not require rejecting every social value or refusing to consider the views of others.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 19. Begging the question & suppressed evidence fallacies work by leaving out a key premise. But the two differs in a sense that the premise that is left in the argument in:

options.text: A. Begging the question fallacy supports a different conclusion in the argument
B. Begging the question fallacy supports the same conclusion in the argument
C. Suppressed evidence fallacy supports the same conclusion in the argument
D. Suppressed evidence fallacy supports a different conclusion in the argument
E. B and D are correct answers
F. A and C are correct answers

logic_JU_1.explanation: The omitted premise in the relevant form of begging the question is one that is needed to support the stated conclusion, while suppressed evidence omits information that would require or support a different conclusion. Therefore statements B and D together give the intended distinction, making E the correct option.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 20. A barrier to critical thinking that uses hasty generalization fallacious tactics is:
logic_JU_1.explanation: Egocentric thinking can lead a person to generalize from personal experience or perspective without adequately considering other evidence or viewpoints. This can produce conclusions that extend beyond what the available evidence supports.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 21. Your brain is made of molecules. Molecules do not have consciousness. Therefore, your brain cannot be the source of consciousness.
logic_JU_1.explanation: The argument transfers a property of the individual parts to the whole. Because the molecules are treated as lacking consciousness, the argument incorrectly concludes that the brain as a whole cannot be associated with consciousness.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 22. Maybe you believe in biological evolution but I don’t believe that my great grandparents were monkeys.
logic_JU_1.explanation: The statement misrepresents biological evolution by portraying it as the claim that a person's great-grandparents were monkeys. Evolutionary theory concerns common ancestry and changes in populations over generations rather than that specific claim.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 23. If we don’t bail out the big automakers, the US economy will collapse. Therefore, we need to bail out the automakers.
logic_JU_1.explanation: The argument uses the threatened consequence of an economic collapse to pressure acceptance of the conclusion. It provides no sufficient evidence that failure to bail out the automakers would necessarily cause the claimed catastrophe, so the frightening consequence functions as the main persuasive force.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 24. It is crazy to think that carrots have feelings. It is crazy to think that cows have feelings. Therefore, vegetarians are just as crazy as fruitarians.
logic_JU_1.explanation: The passage does not establish a sufficiently clear formal or informal fallacy from the statements given. It makes a rhetorical comparison, but the comparison alone does not establish a recognized defect in the argument's logical structure.

logic_JU_1.subject: Logic
logic_JU_1.text: 25. If God did not create the universe, who did?
logic_JU_1.explanation: The question presupposes that the universe was created and frames the issue as though a creator must be identified. It therefore embeds an assumption that has not been established, which is characteristic of a complex question.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 1. In a complex question fallacy we may get questionable ideas either in the part of the premise or in the conclusion. (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: A complex-question fallacy contains a questionable presupposition built into the question itself. It does not require the questionable idea to occur in the premise or conclusion of an argument, so the statement is false.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 2. Lexical definitions are the kinds of definitions found in dictionaries and report the conventional definition of a term for the purpose of eliminating the ambiguity. (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: A lexical definition reports how a word is conventionally used in a language, and dictionaries commonly provide lexical definitions. One important purpose is to clarify established meanings and reduce ambiguity.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 3. Definition by genus and difference is the most effective technique of intentional definitions for producing all types of definitions. (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: Definition by genus and difference is the most generally applicable technique among intensional definitional techniques. It identifies the broader genus and then specifies the characteristics that distinguish the term from other members of that genus.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 4. An intensional definition of a term usually determines the extensional definition of terms and vice versa. (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: Intensional meaning can determine extension because the attributes associated with a term identify the members to which it applies. The reverse does not necessarily hold: listing members or examples can suggest an intension but cannot fully determine it.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 5. The fallacy of composition is committed when we legitimately transfer the attributes of component parts to the whole. (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The fallacy of composition occurs when an attribute of individual parts is improperly transferred to the whole. The transfer is fallacious precisely because what is true of each part does not necessarily follow for the whole.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 1. Identify the statement which is correct about definition in logic. (2022)

options.text: A. All terms under lexical definitions are vague and do not necessarily hold the truth value.
B. The role of definitions is always projected to offer extensional description to the definiendum.
C. In both persuasive and stipulative definitions the ultimate objective is to assign meaning which basically consists of truth.
D. Words are said to be “vague” when there are borderline cases where it is impossible to decide whether they apply, because their meanings do not have sharp boundaries.

logic_UOG_2022.explanation: A term is vague when borderline cases make it impossible to determine clearly whether the term applies. Lexical definitions report established meanings, definitions are not always extensional, and stipulative definitions do not acquire their validity from truth.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 2. A type of definition that assigns meaning of a term as new phenomena/development introduced is ____. (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: A stipulative definition assigns a meaning to a word for the first time and is often introduced when a new phenomenon or development requires a new term or a new meaning. Lexical definitions report existing usage, theoretical definitions relate terms to theories, and persuasive definitions influence attitudes.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 3. Identify the definition which is purely persuasive: (2022)

options.text: A. “Ocean” means those bodies of salt water with an area greater than five million square miles.
C. “Assault” means for legal purpose, a deliberate act resulting in the apprehension of an immediate harmful or offensive contact.

logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The phrase “ruthless self-murdering” uses emotionally charged language intended to create an unfavorable attitude toward the term rather than simply report its meaning. The other definitions are descriptive or technical and do not rely on the same persuasive emotional loading.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 4. Animal experimentation reduces our respect for life. If we don't respect life, we are likely to be more and more tolerant of violent acts like war and murder. Soon our society will become a battlefield in which everyone constantly fears for their lives. It will be the end of civilization. To prevent this terrible consequence, we should make animal experimentation illegal right now. The fallacy here is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The argument presents a chain of increasingly extreme consequences from animal experimentation to widespread violence and the end of civilization without adequately establishing the links between them. This unsupported progression from one event to increasingly severe outcomes is a slippery-slope fallacy.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 5. Which one is wrong about ostensive definition? (2022)

options.text: A. It refers to the examples by means of pointing or by some other gesture.
B. A serious limitation with this method is that it is highly sophisticated.
C. It is among the extensional techniques of defining a term.
D. It is quite important to teach children.

logic_UOG_2022.explanation: Ostensive definition is a simple, primitive form of definition that assigns meaning by pointing to examples or using a gesture. Therefore, describing it as highly sophisticated is incorrect, while the other statements accurately describe its use and classification.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 6. “The devout Mary Cooper has promised to stop gaming and watching television in her house. Thus, Mary must have a gaming and TV addiction problem”. The fallacy here is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: Promising to stop gaming and watching television does not establish that Mary has an addiction. The conclusion goes beyond what the stated evidence supports, so the argument misses the point rather than committing accident, amphiboly, or division.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 7. Which of the following is a sequence of terms is provided in the order of increasing intension? (2022)

options.text: A. Mammal, animal, University of Gondar student, rational animal, student.
B. Animal, mammal, rational animal, student, University of Gondar student.
C. University of Gondar student, student, rational animal, mammal, animal.
D. Animal, rational animal, mammal, student, University of Gondar student.

logic_UOG_2022.explanation: Increasing intension means that each successive term becomes more specific and connotes more attributes. The sequence moves from the broad term “animal” through increasingly specific categories and ends with “University of Gondar student,” which has the greatest intension.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 8. Identify the incorrect statement about a formal fallacy. (2022)

options.text: A. It involves a defect in an argument.
B. It's committed only by deductive arguments.
C. Both inductive and deductive arguments commit this fallacy.
D. It can be identified through its structure.

logic_UOG_2022.explanation: A formal fallacy is identified by a defect in the logical structure or form of an argument and is treated as a defect of deductive reasoning. Therefore, saying that both inductive and deductive arguments commit formal fallacies is the incorrect statement.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 9. Which one of the following is not true about begging the question fallacy? (2022)

options.text: A. This fallacy committed when it conceal a questionably false premise.
B. The conclusion of this argument slightly rephrased the idea of the premise.
C. It deals with the same thing both in the premise and the conclusion.
D. It ignores the third possible alternatives.

logic_UOG_2022.explanation: Begging the question involves assuming the conclusion in the premise, often by restating the same idea in slightly different language. Ignoring third alternatives is characteristic of a false-dichotomy problem, not the defining feature of begging the question.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 10. “Since the average life-span of an individual in Ethiopia is forty-three years, the leaders in this country grow old before they have time to learn the rudiments of good government.” The fallacy in this argument is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The argument applies a broad statistical generalization about life expectancy to a particular group of people in a way that does not follow from the general rule. This inappropriate application of a general principle to a particular case is classified here as accident.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 11. If the American government strengthened security forces in Oregon 2022, then there will be fewer terrorist threats for the fans. There will be fewer terrorist threats for the fans. Thus the American government strengthened security force s in Oregon 2022. What do we say about this argument? (2022)

options.text: A. This argument contains a fallacy of ambiguity.
B. This argument contains no fallacy.
C. This argument contains a formal fallacy.
D. This argument contains a fallacy of grammatical analogy.

logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The argument has the form “If P, then Q; Q; therefore P,” which is the invalid pattern of affirming the consequent. Because the error arises from the logical form of the argument, it is a formal fallacy rather than ambiguity or grammatical analogy.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 12. “Every effort by believers to prove God's existence hasn't been successful. Similarly, atheists' attempts to disprove God's existence have failed. Thus, we have strong grounds to believe in agnosticism”. The fallacy committed here is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The argument treats the failure to prove either theism or atheism as sufficient evidence for accepting agnosticism. Using a lack of proof as the main basis for a conclusion is an appeal to ignorance.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 13. “The Oregon World Athletics Championships were not successful as expected. The major reason is the timing of the event. Clearly, holding such athletic events in the summer is a very bad idea. Summer weather is marked by excessive heat. Thus, the World Athletics Championships should be abolished completely.” The fallacy here is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The premises concern the timing and weather conditions of a particular championship, but the conclusion proposes abolishing the World Athletics Championships entirely. The conclusion goes beyond what the premises establish, so the argument misses the point.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 14. “It’s impossible to be an atheist in a country where 98% of the population professes a belief in God/Allah. Thus, you too should believe in God”. The fallacy here is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The argument appeals to the fact that a large majority of people hold a particular belief and uses that popularity as a reason for accepting it. Popularity does not establish truth, so this is an appeal to the bandwagon.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 15. “Yalemwork Jenberu won the Fana Lamrot music talent show because she made the judges cry. The fallacy here is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The argument treats the judges' emotional reaction as the cause of the contestant's victory without establishing that causal relationship. Inferring a cause from an observed event or sequence without adequate causal evidence is characteristic of post hoc reasoning.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 16. “Rophnan's new album is so dope. Even Mulatu Astatqe, Ethiopia’s most renowned composer, is supposedly impressed by it. The fallacy here is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The argument uses the approval of a highly prestigious or renowned person as the basis for judging the album's quality. Relying on elite status or prestigious approval rather than relevant evidence is an appeal to snobbery.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 17. “You should never marry a feminist. If you do, she will boss you around. She will treat you with contempt and derision. You’ll be separated from your male buddies. You won’t have good sex. So, never marry a feminist”. The fallacy here is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The argument predicts a chain of increasingly negative consequences from marrying a feminist without establishing that one consequence will necessarily lead to the next. This unsupported sequence of escalating outcomes is a slippery-slope fallacy.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 18. A sort of fallacy which is committed when an arguer diverts the attention of the listener by changing the original subject to some slightly different issue— (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: A red herring diverts attention from the original issue by introducing another issue that does not address the argument under discussion. Straw man distorts an opponent's position, while the two ad hominem forms attack the person rather than simply changing the subject.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 19. “Magic is real because I have experienced what can only be described as magical activity”. The type of fallacy committed in this argument is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The argument describes the experience as “magical activity” and then uses that description to support the conclusion that magic is real. The conclusion is therefore assumed in the supporting statement, which makes the reasoning circular or begging the question.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 20. “Her idea that environmental protection needs to be given priority is nonsense. I don’t have a problem to find evidence against her opinion. Just look at her face, she looks like a hungry dog. How this noble idea can be suggested by such an awful faced woman”. The fallacy committed here is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The argument attacks the woman's appearance and insults her instead of addressing her position about environmental protection. Direct verbal abuse of the person in place of addressing the argument is ad hominem abusive, not circumstantial ad hominem, tu quoque, or appeal to force.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 21. “You visit a new country and the first person you meet in the airport is rude. You send a message to a friend back home that everyone in this new country is rude”. The fallacy is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The conclusion about an entire country's population is based on the behavior of only one person. Generalizing from an insufficient or unrepresentative case to a broad class is converse accident, also commonly associated with hasty generalization.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 22. “When women become pregnant, they encounter symptoms such as morning sickness, nausea and vomiting. Yesterday, Mr. Olivier shows the warning sign of pregnancy such as morning sickness, nausea and vomiting. Therefore, Mr. Olivier has become pregnant”. The fallacy is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The argument treats the presence of symptoms associated with pregnancy as sufficient evidence that the symptoms establish pregnancy in this particular case. The causal inference is unsupported, so the argument is classified as a false-cause fallacy rather than a slippery slope, weak analogy, or hasty generalization.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 23. Which one of the following is false? (2022)

options.text: A. Fallacy of relevance is having the wrong kind of evidence.
B. Fallacy of weak induction is having sufficient amount of evidence.
C. Fallacy of presumption is confusion about what the evidence supports.
D. Fallacy of ambiguity is confusion about what the evidence means.

logic_UOG_2022.explanation: A weak-induction fallacy occurs when the evidence is insufficient or too weak to support the conclusion, not when there is a sufficient amount of evidence. The other statements describe the general sources of error associated with relevance, presumption, and ambiguity fallacies.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 24. “Those who are not with us are our enemies” this fallacy is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The statement presents only two possibilities: being with “us” or being an enemy. It excludes other possible positions such as neutrality or partial disagreement, making it a false dichotomy.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 25. “Reptiles include snakes, lizards, and crocodilians”. This definition is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The definition identifies groups or subclasses contained within the broader class of reptiles. A definition by subclass names subclasses, whereas an enumerative definition lists individual members and a precising definition reduces vagueness in a particular context.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 26. “Darwin's theory of evolution is the root cause of many evils with which the world must now cope. The curse of communism, secular humanism, and rock and roll did emerge until after the publication of The Origin of Species”, This fallacy is known as: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The argument treats the appearance of later events after the publication of Darwin's work as evidence that Darwin's theory caused those events. Temporal sequence by itself does not establish causation, so the reasoning commits a false-cause fallacy.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 27. Bhranu: “Based on the arguments I have presented, it is evident that it is morally wrong to use animals for food and clothing.” Aregash: “But you are wearing a leather jacket and you have a roast beef sandwich in your hand. How can you say that using animals for food and clothing is wrong?” The fallacy committed in the above argument is _____. (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: Aregash responds to Bhranu's position by pointing out that Bhranu himself uses animal products rather than addressing the reasons supporting the moral claim. This is the tu quoque, or “you too,” form of ad hominem reasoning.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 28. “If such actions are not illegal, then they would not be prohibited by law”. The fallacy here is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The statement merely restates the conclusion in equivalent terms: something being prohibited by law already expresses that it is illegal. Because the supposed support assumes or repeats the conclusion instead of providing independent evidence, the fallacy is begging the question.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 29. “Stephen Hawking, the world's greatest astrophysicist, claims that the world has already experienced serious greenhouse warming. Therefore, this is probably the case. The fallacy here is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The conclusion is accepted primarily because a famous authority is said to hold the position. The authority's reputation alone does not establish the claim, so relying on that authority rather than adequate supporting evidence constitutes an appeal to unqualified authority.

logic_UOG_2022.subject: Logic
logic_UOG_2022.text: 30. “Of course my opponent is arguing against taxation of the rich. Just look at him! He is the richest person in this town. There is no way someone like that could argue anything else”. The fallacy here is: (2022)
logic_UOG_2022.explanation: The argument dismisses the opponent's position by referring to the opponent's personal circumstances, specifically his wealth, rather than examining the taxation argument. This is ad hominem circumstantial because the person's circumstances are used to discredit the position.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 1. The difference between formal and informal fallacy is, while the former commits due to irrelevant premises to the conclusion, the latter is due to structural defect
logic_WU_1.explanation: The statement reverses the defining characteristics of formal and informal fallacies. A formal fallacy results from a structural defect in the argument, whereas an informal fallacy results from problems involving relevance, ambiguity, presumption, content, or context.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 2. Unlike others, highly educated and intelligent people are never victim to egocentrism.
logic_WU_1.explanation: Egocentrism is the tendency to view issues primarily from one's own perspective, and education or intelligence does not automatically eliminate it. Highly educated and intelligent people can still exhibit egocentric thinking.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 3. Arguments combined by either ...... or are always fallacious irrespective of their truth value of the constituting premises.
logic_WU_1.explanation: An argument using an either-or structure is not automatically fallacious. A disjunctive argument can be logically valid when its alternatives and premises properly support the conclusion.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 4. All informal fallacies are created because of the premises of an argument which are logically irrelevant with a conclusion.
logic_WU_1.explanation: Informal fallacies are not all caused by irrelevant premises. They can also result from ambiguity, unjustified assumptions, weak evidence, improper causal reasoning, or other problems involving the content and context of an argument.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 5. All fallacies of relevance are committed when there is no logical connection between the premises and the conclusion
logic_WU_1.explanation: Fallacies of relevance occur when the premises fail to provide logically relevant support for the conclusion. The premises may appear persuasive, but they do not establish the conclusion being argued for.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 6. Admission of fallibility is a positive sign of interest for fair resolution of the issue.
logic_WU_1.explanation: Recognizing one's own fallibility supports intellectual humility and fair evaluation of arguments. It encourages a person to consider evidence, acknowledge mistakes, and revise conclusions when appropriate.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 7. Appeal to force fallacy involves a threat by the arguer to the physical or psychological well-being of the listener or the reader.
logic_WU_1.explanation: Appeal to force attempts to establish a conclusion through a threat rather than relevant evidence. The threat may concern physical, psychological, social, or other forms of harm.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 8. The fallacy of division falsely argues that what is true of the whole must be true of its individual parts.
logic_WU_1.explanation: The statement describes the fallacy of composition, which incorrectly transfers a property of a whole to its individual parts. The fallacy of division makes the opposite error by transferring a property of the whole to its parts.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 1. The question of connections
logic_WU_1.explanation: Relevance concerns whether there is a logical connection between the premises and the conclusion. The question of connections therefore corresponds to relevance.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 2. Ability to reason properly
logic_WU_1.explanation: Correctness concerns whether reasoning conforms to appropriate standards of sound thinking. The ability to reason properly therefore corresponds to correctness.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 3. Open mindedness and impartiality
logic_WU_1.explanation: Fairness requires considering relevant perspectives without allowing personal preferences or prejudices to distort judgment. Open-mindedness and impartiality are therefore associated with fairness.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 4. Free of obscurity and vagueness
logic_WU_1.explanation: Clarity requires ideas to be expressed in an understandable way without unnecessary obscurity or vagueness. A clear argument allows the reader or listener to understand exactly what is being claimed.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 5. Ability to think deeply
logic_WU_1.explanation: Completeness requires examining the relevant dimensions of an issue sufficiently rather than stopping at a superficial treatment. Deep thinking therefore corresponds to completeness.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 6. Being exact, accurate and careful
logic_WU_1.explanation: Precision concerns expressing information with sufficient exactness and specificity. Being exact, accurate, and careful therefore corresponds to precision.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 7. Behaving in the same way or manner
logic_WU_1.explanation: Consistency means maintaining coherence rather than changing standards or positions without justification. Behaving in the same way or manner therefore corresponds to consistency.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 8. Provision of correct information
logic_WU_1.explanation: Accuracy means that information corresponds correctly to the facts or evidence. Providing correct information therefore corresponds to accuracy.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 1. From the following which informal fallacies are purely find in the same groups?

options.text: A. suppressed evidence, false dichotomy, complex question and begging question
B. division, composition, amphiboly and equivocation
C. appeal to pity, appeal to force, appeal to ignorance & appeal to unqualified authority
D. false cause, false dichotomy, suppressed question and weak analogy

logic_WU_1.explanation: Appeal to pity, appeal to force, appeal to ignorance, and appeal to unqualified authority are all classified as fallacies of relevance. The other choices combine fallacies from different categories, including presumption, ambiguity, causal reasoning, and weak analogy.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 2. One of the following alternatives is correctly matched regarding barriers of critical thinking
logic_WU_1.explanation: Relativistic thinking can treat truth as subjective, and unsupported assumptions can include wishful thinking. Sociocentrism is associated with group-centered thinking rather than superiority bias, while egocentrism is associated with self-centered thinking rather than group conformity.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 3. Which of the following statement is correctly paired with type of informal fallacy it committed?

options.text: A. “Of course, you must believe in god existence, because eighty five percent of Ethiopians believes it........ Bandwagon”
B. Do you want to have modern shoes? Then, you should choose Ambessa Shoe Factory. This is because our products are the first choice of the famous athlete Haile G/Selassie........Appeal to snobbery

C. Abay insurance company is not for all rater for thus who are responsible for their families future. Thus if you are responsible parent you should be a part of our insurance company.........Apple to vanity

D. My teacher told me that cheating on exam is a bad habit. But he himself told me that he used to cheat on exam when he was in university. Therefore, his argument is foolish........ad hominiem circumstantial

logic_WU_1.explanation: A is bandwagon because the claim is supported by the supposed majority view. C appeals to vanity by associating the decision with being a responsible parent, and D uses circumstantial ad hominem by attacking the teacher's behavior instead of addressing the argument. B relies on a celebrity endorsement, but merely citing a famous athlete does not establish the appeal-to-snobbery fallacy.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 4. “Contemporary philosophers contributed more for the development of Logic. Plato and Parmenides were contemporary philosophers. Therefore, Plato and Parmenides contributed more for the development of Logic.” Which of the following is true about the above passage

options.text: A. It commits fallacy of equivocation
B. It can mislead the reader or listener
C. it bears error in language usage
D. It is a good argument

logic_WU_1.explanation: The argument equivocates on the meaning of “contemporary.” The term is used in different senses, creating a shift in meaning between the premise and conclusion. This makes the argument an example of equivocation rather than a sound argument.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 5. “Wolkite University is not well organized. Therefore, every course offered in this university is not well organized.” The type of the fallacy is
logic_WU_1.explanation: The argument commits division because it transfers a property attributed to the whole university to every individual course offered by that university. Division occurs when a property of a whole is incorrectly assumed to belong to each of its parts.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 6. “Ethnic conflict is one of the problems of Africa. Hence, to create peace and stability in Africa, ethnic diversity should be replaced by ethnic homogeneity.”
logic_WU_1.explanation: The argument identifies ethnic conflict as a problem but concludes that ethnic diversity itself should be eliminated without establishing that diversity is the cause of the conflict or that homogeneity is the appropriate solution. The conclusion therefore misses the point that must be established by the premises.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 7. “Researchers have shown that women's have more accurate intuition than men do. The reason cited is that men's intuition is more often mistaken.”

options.text: B. Fallacy of begging the question
D. None causa pro causa fallacy

logic_WU_1.explanation: The stated reason that men's intuition is more often mistaken essentially restates the conclusion that women's intuition is more accurate rather than providing independent support. Treating the conclusion as its own justification is the fallacy of begging the question.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 8. “Dancing is the work of the devil! If we let young people listen and dance to rock music, tell you that sooner or later they will turn against their parents, they will take to fornications and pornography, and they will grow up to be prostitutes. No good can come from dancing. So I have cancelled all the future dances.”
logic_WU_1.explanation: The argument predicts a chain of increasingly serious consequences from allowing young people to listen to and dance to rock music. It assumes that the initial action will inevitably lead to those extreme outcomes, which characterizes the slippery slope fallacy.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 9. Shewit: “it is morally wrong to use animals for food and clothes.” Derartu: “but you like to wear a leather jacket and your favorite food is meat. How can you say that using animals for food and clothing is wrong?”

options.text: A. Ad hominem tu quo que

logic_WU_1.explanation: Derartu responds to Shewit's claim by pointing to Shewit's own behavior rather than addressing whether the claim itself is correct. This is the tu quoque form of ad hominem, which attacks an alleged inconsistency in the speaker.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 10. “An instant has no duration. But an hour is composed of instants. Therefore, an hour has no duration”
logic_WU_1.explanation: The argument transfers a property of individual parts to the whole composed of those parts. It concludes that an hour has no duration because an individual instant is treated as having no duration, which is the fallacy of composition.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 11. “The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopian constitution provided the right to vote for all citizens of the state. Therefore, children have the right to vote.”
logic_WU_1.explanation: The argument applies a general statement about citizens to children without establishing that the general statement applies to children in the claimed way. Applying a general principle improperly to a particular case is the fallacy of accident.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 12. “Aljazeera and CNN are global news media. They were disseminated false information to the international community regarding the ongoing war between TPLF and Ethiopian forces. Based on the aforesaid evidence we can conclude that nowadays global news media are not spreading true information.”
logic_WU_1.explanation: The conclusion makes a broad claim about global news media based on claims about only two organizations. Drawing a general conclusion from too few cases is a hasty generalization.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 13. “The operation of a camera is similar in many ways to the operation of an eye. If you are to see anything in a darkened room, the pupils of your eyes must first dilate. Accordingly, if you are to take a photograph (without flash) in a darkened room, the apparatus of the camera lens must first be opened.”
logic_WU_1.explanation: The argument infers that because the eye and camera share some similarities, the same specific operation must apply in the relevant situation. The similarities are insufficient to establish the conclusion, making this a weak analogy.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 14. Mr. Lincoln, are you saying that President Bush made a moral error when he decided to go to war with Iraq? I cannot believe my ears. That’s not how Americans feel. Not true Americans, anyway. You are an American, aren’t you, Ms. Lincoln?
logic_WU_1.explanation: The argument appeals to what Americans supposedly believe instead of addressing whether the decision to go to war was morally correct. Using popular opinion as support for a conclusion is an appeal to the people.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 15. “Whenever I wear green T-shirt my logic grade goes up. That why I lave my green T-shirt to wear only on the days of the exam”

options.text: A. Not the cause for the cause
B. After this, therefore, because of this
D. Post hoc ergo propter hoc

logic_WU_1.explanation: The argument assumes that wearing the green T-shirt causes the higher grade merely because the two events are associated. Inferring causation from temporal or coincidental association without sufficient evidence is post hoc ergo propter hoc.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 16. The famous artist Yirdaw Tenaw said that “watching football of English premier league on DS TV is interesting and a good entertainment for weekend”
logic_WU_1.explanation: The statement relies on the opinion of a famous artist as support for the quality of a television entertainment service without establishing relevant expertise. Relying on an authority who lacks relevant expertise is an appeal to unqualified authority.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 1. The prosecutor can’t find any reasonable explanation for why my dad was died. See! See! That proves that he was poisoned! (2 pts)
logic_WU_1.answer: Appeal to ignorance fallacy. The absence of a reasonable alternative explanation does not prove that the father was poisoned.
logic_WU_1.explanation: The argument treats the lack of a known alternative explanation as proof that poisoning occurred. The failure to establish another explanation does not by itself establish that poisoning occurred.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 2. Everything that runs has feet. The Abay River runs very quickly. Therefore, Abay River has feet. (2 pts)
logic_WU_1.answer: Equivocation fallacy. The word “runs” is used with different meanings: running with feet and flowing as a river.
logic_WU_1.explanation: The argument changes the meaning of “runs” between its premises and conclusion. Running as an activity performed by something with feet is different from a river running in the sense of flowing, so the argument equivocates on the word.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 3. A few minutes after Prime Minster Dr. Abiy Ahmed finished his speech on open public stage on June 23, a devastating hand bomb explosion struck at Addis Ababa. For the safety of the people up there, it is imperative that Prime Minster Dr. Abiy Ahmed make no more public speeches. (2 pts)
logic_WU_1.answer: Post hoc ergo propter hoc fallacy. The argument assumes that because the explosion occurred shortly after the speech, the speech caused the explosion or establishes that future speeches will cause similar danger.
logic_WU_1.explanation: The argument infers causation from temporal sequence alone. The fact that the explosion occurred shortly after the speech does not establish that the speech caused the explosion or that future public speeches will produce the same event.

logic_WU_1.subject: logic
logic_WU_1.text: 4. Write the difference between the fallacy of weak induction & fallacy of presumption. (4 pts)
logic_WU_1.answer: A fallacy of weak induction occurs when the premises provide insufficient or weak evidential support for the conclusion, even though the premises may be relevant to it. A fallacy of presumption occurs when an argument depends on an unjustified assumption or takes something for granted instead of adequately establishing it.
logic_WU_1.explanation: Weak induction concerns insufficient evidential support: the premises may be relevant but are not strong enough to justify the conclusion. Presumption concerns an unjustified assumption built into the reasoning, such as assuming what needs to be established or relying on information that has not been adequately supported.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 1. There are many religions than ever before in the country and there are also many religious conflicts than ever before. Therefore, to avoid the conflict we have to completely destroy all religions. This fallacy belongs to:
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The argument treats the existence of multiple religions as the single cause of religious conflict and assumes that eliminating religion would eliminate the conflict. This oversimplifies a complex situation by ignoring other possible causes.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 2. Which one of the following is true about a categorical proposition of “Some S are not P”?

options.text: A. Its truth value in obversion is same
B. Its obversion is “Some P are not non S”
D. Its conversion is “Some S are not P”

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The obversion of a proposition preserves its truth value. “Some S are not P” is an O-proposition, and its obverse is “Some S are non-P.”

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 3. People often use emotive terminology in their arguments, BECAUSE:

options.text: A. They want to make value claims about the subject matter of their arguments without providing genuine evidence.
B. They want to paralyze the logical thought processes of readers/listeners, and thus prevent them from seeing any logical deficiency in their arguments.
C. Human beings are naturally governed by their emotional instincts.

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: Emotive terminology can be used to express value judgments without providing evidence and to influence the emotional response of an audience. Therefore, both A and B are correct, making D the appropriate choice.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 4. Which one of the following is incorrect about the fallacies of Straw Man and Red Herring?

options.text: A. While Red Herring always makes conclusion about the original argument, Straw Man usually prefers to keep silent on that respect.
B. Straw Man manages to distort the original argument by stretching the argument to its extreme end whereas the method of Red Herring is confined to ignoring the whole matter.
C. Both Red Herring and Straw Man tend to lead the reader or listener off the original argument though they do it in a manner that is somewhat different.
D. Both fallacies involve emotional appeal towards the reader or the listener.
E. Both fallacies make conclusion by generating new premises.

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: Straw Man and Red Herring are forms of irrelevant diversion, but emotional appeal is not an essential feature of either fallacy. Straw Man distorts an opponent’s position, while Red Herring diverts attention to an irrelevant issue.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 5. “It is not hard to see the impact of religion in society. In the 7th & 10th church attendance fell by as much as 30%. During that same period, we saw an increase in common-law living, abortion, & inner-city crime. So, no doubt, if we want to get society back on the rails, we must return to our religious roots.”

options.text: E. Post hoc ergo propter hoc

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The argument presents selected evidence about church attendance and social conditions while leaving out other relevant evidence and possible explanations. Suppressing relevant evidence can make the conclusion appear stronger than the available evidence supports.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 6. The Constitution guarantees freedom of speech for everyone. Therefore, citizens have a right to disseminate fake news.
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The premise about freedom of speech does not establish the specific conclusion that citizens have an unrestricted right to disseminate fake news. The conclusion therefore goes beyond what the premise establishes.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 7. When we say intensional meaning determines extension, we mean one of the following:

options.text: A. The intensional meaning of a term serves as the criterion for deciding what the members are.
B. Rules of the ordinary language can be used to give an extension of the intension of a term.
C. Extensional meaning suggests intensional meaning.

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: Intensional meaning gives the defining characteristics or criteria associated with a term. Those criteria determine which objects fall within the term's extension.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 8. Of the following statements, one is FALSE about definitions.

options.text: A. The definiendum represents the word or term that is proposed to be defined.
B. Strictly speaking, both stipulative and theoretical definitions are neither true nor false.
C. Definition by genus and difference can be used as a technique for producing lexical, stipulative, theoretical, and persuasive definitions, but cannot for producing precise definitions.
D. Although persuasive definitions may be evaluated as either true or false, their primary issue is neither truth nor falsity, but effectiveness.

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: Persuasive definitions are primarily designed to influence attitudes rather than to establish truth or falsity. Their effectiveness in shaping attitudes is therefore their central concern.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 9. The fallacy in which the arguer attempts to create a mob mentality is:
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: Appeal to the people attempts to persuade by exploiting popular opinion or group pressure. Creating a mob mentality is a characteristic example of this appeal.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 10. A kind of fallacy that associates the product with selected few group who are pursued is:
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: Appeal to snobbery associates a product or idea with an exclusive or socially prestigious group. The appeal attempts to persuade by encouraging identification with that selected group.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 11. “Foal” means a young horse. What is the technique of this definition?

options.text: C. Definition by genus and difference

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: A synonymous definition explains a term by giving an expression with the same meaning. “Young horse” supplies the meaning of “foal” directly.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 12. A kind of fallacy whereby the second arguer attempts to make the first arguer appear to be hypocritical or arguing in bad faith, & usually accomplishes this by citing features in the life or behavior of the first arguer that conflict with the latter’s conclusion is:
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: Tu quoque is a form of ad hominem in which an arguer responds to criticism by accusing the critic of hypocrisy or inconsistency. The attack concerns the first arguer's behavior rather than the merits of the argument.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 13. “Ending one’s own life is morally permissible because people are rightfully in charge of their own lives. And this is so because people have the freedom to determine their own destiny. And this follows from the fact that people have the moral right to decide whether they live or die. And this is true because ending one’s own life is morally permissible.” The fallacy committed in this argument is:
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The argument assumes the conclusion that ending one's own life is morally permissible while using that same conclusion as support for the reasoning. This circular structure is the fallacy of begging the question.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 14. The definition “Rest” means (1) the repose of sleep, (2) an interval of silence between notes, (3) a period of inactivity” is an example of:
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: An enumerative definition identifies a term by listing the different cases or meanings to which it applies. The definition of “Rest” lists several distinct meanings of the word.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 15. The definition “Blogger” means an egocentric individual who wastes inordinate amounts of time writing nonsense opinions on websites that nobody reads” is an example of:
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The definition uses strongly evaluative expressions such as “egocentric” and “nonsense” to influence the audience's attitude. Such emotionally loaded language is characteristic of a persuasive definition.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 16. Which of the following is included in the intensional meaning of the word “Ocean”?

options.text: E. All of the above, except “C”

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: Intensional meaning consists of characteristics associated with a term. “Salty” describes a characteristic, whereas Atlantic, Mediterranean, and Pacific are particular members within the extension of ocean.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 17. Which of the following are both intensional definitions?

options.text: A. Definition by genus and difference, enumerative definition
B. Definition by genus and difference, definition by subclass

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: Definition by genus and difference and definition by subclass identify conceptual characteristics or relationships. These are therefore intensional rather than merely enumerative or ostensive definitions.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 18. When an arguer ignores some important piece of evidence that outweighs the presented evidence and arrives at a very different conclusion, the person commits fallacy of:
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: Suppressed evidence occurs when important relevant evidence is omitted from an argument. Ignoring evidence that could significantly affect the conclusion can therefore produce a misleading inference.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 19. The saying “If you have a dream, you should not sleep!” is unacceptable for dreaming is impossible without a sleep. This fallacy committed is?
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The statement shifts between different meanings of “dream”: an aspiration or goal and an experience during sleep. Using the same term in different senses creates equivocation.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 20. Which one of the following statements is true?

options.text: A. The primary aim of precising definition is to influence the attitude of the readers
B. A theoretical definition is primarily intended to reduce the vagueness of the word
C. Lexical definition can be evaluated as more interesting or fruitful with reference to the actual usage of the word
D. Stipulative definition is used to set up secret codes in areas of military expression and other related developments

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: A lexical definition reports the established meaning and usage of a word. Its adequacy can therefore be considered with reference to actual language use.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 21. This exam is difficult. Therefore, every question in this exam is difficult. The defect of this argument is committing the fallacy of:
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The argument transfers a property attributed to the whole exam to every individual question. This improper transfer from the whole to its parts is the fallacy of composition.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 22. As a lexical definition, the definition “Practical” means not being impractical” may be criticized as:

options.text: C. Failing to indicate the context to which the definition pertains

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The definition explains “Practical” by stating what it is not rather than by describing its positive characteristics. It is therefore a negative definition.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 23. Which of the following series of terms is put in an order of increasing extension?

options.text: A. Meta Beer- Ethiopian Beer- Beer- Alcoholic Drink- Beverage
B. Alcoholic Drink- Beverage- Beer- Ethiopian Beer- Meta Beer
C. Beverage- Alcoholic Drink- Beer- Ethiopian Beer- Meta Beer
D. Ethiopian Beer- Meta Beer- Alcoholic Drink- Beverage- Beer
E. Beer- Ethiopian Beer- Meta Beer- Alcoholic Drink- Beverage

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: Increasing extension moves from a narrower class to a broader class. Meta Beer is narrower than Ethiopian Beer, which is narrower than Beer, Alcoholic Drink, and Beverage.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 24. Some non-A are B. No non-A are B. For the above proposition, determine how the new statement is related to the given statement and determine the truth value of the new statement. Adopt the Aristotelian standpoint and assume that “A” and “B” denote things that actually exist.
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: “Some non-A are B” is a particular affirmative proposition, while “No non-A are B” is a universal negative proposition. They are contradictory because they cannot both be true and cannot both be false; if the first is true, the second is false.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 25. Among the following, which one is the basic pattern of standard-form statements?

options.text: B. Quantifier - Subject Term - Predicate Term
C. Subject Term - Copula - Predicate Term
D. Quantifier - Subject Term - Copula - Predicate Term

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: A standard-form categorical proposition contains a quantifier, subject term, copula, and predicate term. These components establish its quantity, subject, relationship, and predicate.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 26. One of the following can be granted with certainty about collective predication of attributes

options.text: A. It always results in the fallacy of Division or Composition
B. It means the attribute in question is possessed by each and every member of the class
C. A collective predication of an attribute can only result in a fallacy if it’s succeeded by an erroneous transference of attribute from the part-members to the whole/class or vice versa
D. We can only envisage the existence of such predication in the conclusion of an argument
E. Sometimes we find collectively predicated attributes in the fallacy of Accident

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: Collective predication concerns a group considered as a whole and is not automatically fallacious. A fallacy arises when an attribute is improperly transferred between the whole and its members.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 27. “So long as we are given up to the throe of desires with the constant hopes and fears, so long as we are the subjects of willing, we can never have lasting happiness and peace.” Of the following conclusions made on the basis of the above premise, only one can be granted without risking the fallacy of missing the point.

options.text: A. We should try to control our desires if we are to attain happiness
B. We should stop willing altogether so that we may be happy
C. Since we can never stop wanting and wanting results in fear, we might as well end our lives
D. We better stop trying to be happy since that is beyond our grasp
E. Happiness is an overrated concept which a willing being, like man, should not expect to achieve

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The premise connects lasting happiness with freedom from the constant effects of desire, hope, and fear. Controlling desires is therefore the conclusion most directly related to the stated premise.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 28. One of the following is not a standard of critical thinking.
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: Precision, accuracy, and consistency are standards used to evaluate reasoning. Socio-centrism is not a standard of critical thinking.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 29. Ethiopia has never been colonized. Alemu is an Ethiopian. Hence Alemu has never been colonized. Which one of the following is true of the above argument?

options.text: A. The attribute is predicated distributively.
B. The argument commits the fallacy of Accident
C. There is a legitimate transference of attribute from the class to the members.
D. The argument commits Composition fallacy.
E. The argument commits the fallacy of Division

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The argument transfers a property of Ethiopia considered as a whole to an individual Ethiopian. An improper transfer of an attribute from a whole or class to its members is the fallacy of division.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 30. A proposition/statement that makes an assertion about every member of its subject class is:
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: A universal proposition makes an assertion about every member of its subject class. A particular proposition concerns some members, while a singular proposition concerns an individual.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 1. A formal fallacy is an error in reasoning that involves the explicit use of an invalid form.
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: A formal fallacy is an error in the logical structure or form of an argument. The invalid form makes the inference logically defective.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 2. Although all fallacious arguments are either unsound or uncogent, unsound and uncogent arguments may sometimes be free from fallacy.
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: An argument can be unsound or uncogent without necessarily containing a recognized fallacious form. Unsoundness and uncogency concern the overall quality of an argument, whereas a fallacy identifies a specific error in reasoning.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 3. Informal fallacies often occur out of malice on the part of the arguer who presents bad arguments as if they are good.
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: Informal fallacies do not require malicious intent. They can result from mistakes, misunderstanding, poor evidence, ambiguity, or faulty reasoning.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 4. The fallacy of amphiboly occurs when a single word is used in two different senses in the same argument.
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: Amphiboly results from ambiguity in the grammatical structure of a sentence. Using a word in two different senses is characteristic of equivocation.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 5. The quality of a universal proposition is determined by its quantifier.
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The quantifier determines the quantity of a proposition. Its quality is determined by whether the proposition is affirmative or negative.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 1. When water is poured on the top of a pile of rocks, it always trickles down to the rocks on the bottom. Similarly, when rich people make lots of money, we can expect this money to trickle down to the poor.
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The argument compares water flowing through rocks with money moving through an economy. The relevant similarities are insufficient to establish the conclusion, making this a weak analogy.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 2. Abebe says to Tessema, “You are needlessly hard on your children,” and Tessema responds by saying that, “you don’t have the right to say that, it was only yesterday that one of your children was crying herself to death because you prohibited her from going to a party.”
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: Tessema responds to criticism by pointing to Abebe's own behavior instead of addressing whether the criticism is correct. This is the tu quoque fallacy.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 3. The FBI and the CIA failed to prevent the terrorist attack on the World Trade Center. Therefore, these government agencies should be abolished immediately.
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The argument treats the agencies' failure to prevent an attack as sufficient reason to abolish them. That conclusion is not established by the premise and involves an unsupported causal inference.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 4. San Diego has the same latitude as Yuma and Arizona, and San Diego enjoys moderate temperatures through the summer months. Therefore, probably Yuma enjoys moderate temperatures through the summer months.
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The argument relies primarily on shared latitude while ignoring other major factors affecting climate, such as elevation and proximity to the ocean. The comparison is therefore insufficient to support the conclusion.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 5. Developed countries have the moral obligation to assist poor developing countries because most of the developing countries consist of people who earn $1 a day and many people die of common diseases in these countries.
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The argument emphasizes poverty, very low income, and deaths from disease to evoke sympathy in support of its conclusion. This reliance on emotional sympathy characterizes an appeal to pity.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 1. The Converse of the following set of Venn diagram is
logic_AASTU_1.figure: The given Venn diagram shows two overlapping circles with the left-only region shaded.

options.text: A. Two overlapping circles with an X in the intersection.
B. Two overlapping circles with the intersection shaded.
C. Two overlapping circles with an X in the left-only region.
D. Two overlapping circles with the right-only region shaded.
E. Two overlapping circles with no marked region.

logic_AASTU_1.explanation: The given diagram shades the portion belonging only to the left circle. Taking the converse exchanges the two terms, so the corresponding right-only portion is shaded.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 2. Draw and fill the Venn diagram for the following statement (Boolean standpoint) “Some S are not P”.
logic_AASTU_1.answer: Draw two overlapping circles labeled S and P and place an X in the part of S that lies outside P.
logic_AASTU_1.figure: Two overlapping circles labeled S and P, with an X in the S-only region.
logic_AASTU_1.explanation: “Some S are not P” asserts that at least one member belongs to S but does not belong to P. In a Venn diagram, this is represented by placing an X in the portion of S outside the intersection with P.

logic_AASTU_1.subject: logic
logic_AASTU_1.text: 3. Given the categorical proposition: “No Ethiopians are Europeans”. A. Contrapose the categorical proposition. B. Draw Venn Diagram for the contraposition. C. Determine the validity of the immediate inference. D. If the argument is not valid then which fallacy is committed?
logic_AASTU_1.answer: A. No non-Europeans are non-Ethiopians. B. Draw a Venn diagram with the intersection of non-Europeans and non-Ethiopians shaded. C. The immediate inference is invalid. D. The fallacy is illicit contraposition.
